feedback:
Approved because only one run remains this iteration. A revise would need a revision and a second review before the race, which the budget cannot fit, so the iteration would end unscored. Nothing below states how this candidate will perform.

Evidence: iteration 1 (ki 0.4) scored 62.18, the best so far. Iteration 2 (ki 1.0, otherwise identical) scored 59.93. Every run in all three iterations went off track with exactly one line-loss event, max_error sat at the 0.06 m limit, and progress stayed between 0.11 and 0.17. Steering oscillation stayed between 0.07 and 0.15. The gain sweep changed progress very little, so gains are not the limiting factor. The failure is tied to the line being lost once early and the robot then drifting off.

Check before racing: the rationale describes outer sensors widened to x = ±0.045 m, but the geometry field still shows ±0.03 m. If the built candidate has the old array, this race only repeats iteration 2 and tells us nothing new about sensor placement. Please confirm the widened positions are in the build.

What to do with the next race, which is the last one this iteration:
- If line_loss_events drops to 0 or near 0 and progress rises above about 0.3, keep the wider array and revisit base_speed for completion_time.
- If progress stays near 0.17 with one loss per run, the widened array did not fix the failure. Next iteration, revert to the ±0.03 m array with ki 1.0 and test line_loss as search_right, or check initial alignment.
- If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 with the wider array, reduce kp to 2.0 as the rationale suggests.
requested_changes: Confirm the geometry matches the rationale: outer sensors at x = ±0.045 m and inner sensors at ±0.0225 m, with the same 5-sensor layout, since the current geometry field still shows ±0.03 m.

If the wider array still gives one line-loss event per run with progress near 0.17, revert to ±0.03 m with ki 1.0 and test line_loss = search_right against last_direction, because iteration 2 left the line-loss behaviour untested.

If any run finishes, read completion_time: at 2.8 s or above, raise base_speed from 1.4 toward 1.5 to 1.6. Iteration 2 showed no finishes, so do not change base_speed before there is completion evidence.
